newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade light at $65-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade light at $65-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales were slow at $65.00 per cwt, unchanged from last week's massive volume, feedlot sources said.
About 300 heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in Kansas and about 1,500 steers and heifers sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, sources said.
Packer bids at $64.00 to $65.00 were passed by the majority of owners who priced their cattle at $66.00 to $67.00, with some at $68.00, they said.
Fed cattle prices were seen trading at $66.00 on Wednesday if beef prices remain strong, several cattle feeders said.
Beef prices Tuesday closed up $0.61 to $1.07 per cwt, with 231 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $105.62, up $0.81 from Monday and up $3.08 since prices started trending higher after Wednesday's close, USDA statistics showed.
Support in beef was tied to last-minute buying to top off retail freezers for pre-Labor Day holiday beef promotions, market sources said.
Labor Day, September 1, is the final holiday of the summer and usually a strong demand period for beef for outdoor cookouts during the three-day holiday weekend.
